content:
emily: FYI we have an Acme Analytics escalation — their requests are getting routed to us-east resulting in 200-400ms extra p99. They say they set region header to eu-west but backend logs show us-east. Ticket: #ACME-4923

emily: quick reproduction they gave:
```bash
curl -v "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?region=us-east" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \n  -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west" \n  -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```

emily: request_id=01H4ZK2JX9-req-77 in our logs, routing decision record attached (see trace). They claim SDK 0.9.2 which they just updated from.

raj: thanks. can you paste the routing trace lines for that req id? specifically kernel:route_decision and any header/param parsing logs.

emily: pasted excerpt from trace:
```
[2026-02-27T15:02:11Z] req=01H4ZK2JX9 headers={Authorization:***, X-Client-Region=eu-west} query={region=us-east} route_decision=us-east reason=client_param
[2026-02-27T15:02:11Z] resolved_model=redwood-llama-70b@us-east
```

emily: they also sent a HAR; shows both header and query param present.

laura: quick context: older routing precedence was query param > header because of a legacy migration flag. we changed that in routing v0.10 to prefer explicit header when present, but the flag was off for customers on older routing configs.

raj: ah — so if the customer is on the routing-family tagged pre-v0.10, query param will win. do we know how many of their calls hit the legacy edge? maybe due to CDN edge TTL?

emily: looks like ~35% of their traffic in the last hour hit edges with the legacy flag (edge-version: 2025-11-12).

raj: repro steps for us to confirm locally: use the exact curl above, then hit our debug endpoint to dump routing precedence:
```bash
curl -H "X-Debug: routing" "https://edge-debug.redwood.ai/debug?req=01H4ZK2JX9"
```
This should show precedence_order=[query_param, header, geo] for legacy edges.

laura: proposed mitigation: add temporary override rule at the global router to treat X-Client-Region as authoritative when present for the Acme tenant. small canary: apply to tenant_id=acme-42 for 10% of requests first. then roll to 100%.

raj: I can implement a routing policy change: add rule_id=route-override-acme-2026-02-27 with condition tenant==acme-42 && header_exists(X-Client-Region) -> set route_key=X-Client-Region. Will push to canary.

emily: Mark (customer) — are you OK with us overriding on your account? this won't change billing, just routing precedence.

mark_acme: yes please, makes sense. we've got bursts from eu users and seeing bad p99. go ahead. thx. :pray:

deploy-bot: Starting canary deployment route-override-acme-2026-02-27 -> 10% traffic (edge pool eu-west). ID: deploy-9832

laura: monitor p99 latency and error rates for 15 minutes. watch for any routing loops or 5xx. If anything odd, revert rule via rollback deploy-9832.

raj: canary deployed. quick smoke logs show requests with both header+param now routing to eu-west when header present. snippet:
```
[2026-02-27T15:08:04Z] req=01H4ZK2JX9 headers={X-Client-Region=eu-west, region=us-east} route_decision=eu-west reason=header_override_rule(route-override-acme-2026-02-27)
```

emily: customer reporting immediate improvement — p99 dropped ~230ms.

deploy-bot: Canary complete -> promoted to 100% for tenant acme-42. deploy-9832 -> success

laura: follow-ups: 1) patch the SDK docs to warn about query param vs header precedence for versions <0.10, 2) reach out to edge CDN team about TTLs for routing-config metadata, 3) schedule automatic tenant config migration to latest routing family.

emily: created follow-up tasks: DOCS-1182, CDN-1190, MIGRATE-ACME-42. Also updated ticket #ACME-4923 with notes + fix. closing slack thread. :white_check_mark:
